---
title: "Figure 1.3.1: Exports of Goods"
---

![Python: `python/fig-1-3-1.py`](../images/python/fig-1-3-1.png)

Two panels. Each shows bars (percent of GDP, left scale) and open circles
(percent of exports, right scale) for Mexico and Canada.

**New in this chart:**

- two panels drawn by one loop;
- a different colour for each bar;
- circles as markers;
- a legend with symbols that do not appear in the chart in that form.

## The data

Two sheets, one per panel, each with 2 rows:

| Sheet | category | bar column | circle column |
|---|---|---|---|
| `datal` | Mexico, Canada | `(% GDP)` | `(% goods exports)` |
| `datar` | Mexico, Canada | `Percent of GDP` | `Percent of exports (right scale)` |

The two sheets use different column names for the same concepts, because the
two Excel charts were set up differently. The script records the names per
panel.

## The script

### Describing the panels

```python
bar_colours = {"Mexico": "#08649B", "Canada": "#CB6418"}

# Each panel: (data sheet, panel title, bar column, circle column).
panels = [
    ("datal", "Canada and Mexico Exports\nto the United States",
     "(% GDP)", "(% goods exports)"),
    ("datar", "United States Exports to\nCanada and Mexico",
     "Percent of GDP", "Percent of exports (right scale)"),
]
```

Everything that differs between the two panels is collected in a list, one
entry per panel. See [Several panels](../techniques.qmd#sec-panels).
`bar_colours` maps the *category* (not a series) to a colour, because here
each bar has its own colour.

```python
fig, axes = new_chart(
    title="Exports of Goods",
    subtitle=None,
    ...
    top_gap=0.55,
    bottom_gap=0.45,
    ncols=2,
    wspace=0.75,
)
```

- **Panels.** `ncols=2` returns a list of two plot areas, 0.75 inches apart.
- **Room for panel titles.** There is no subtitle, and `top_gap=0.55` leaves
  room for the panel titles above each plot.

### Drawing each panel

```python
for ax, (sheet, panel_title, bar_column, circle_column) in zip(axes, panels):
    data = read_chart_data(STEM, sheet)
    x = range(len(data))

    # Bars: percent of GDP, on the left scale.
    ax.bar(x, data[bar_column], width=0.56,
           color=[bar_colours[c] for c in data["category"]])
```

`zip(axes, panels)` pairs the first plot area with the first panel
description, and the second with the second. The description is unpacked
into four names in the `for` line.

`color=` accepts a list with one colour per bar. The list comprehension looks
up the colour of each category in turn: `["#08649B", "#CB6418"]`.

```python
    ax.set_title(panel_title, loc="left", color="#7F7F7F", fontweight="bold",
                 fontsize=11.5, linespacing=0.95, pad=14)
```

`set_title` puts a title above one plot area. In the REO style, panel titles
are grey, bold and left-aligned. `pad=14` raises the title 14 points above
the plot.

```python
    # Circles: percent of exports, on the right scale.
    ax_right = add_right_axis(ax, (0, 100), 25)
    ax_right.tick_params(axis="y", direction="in", length=2.3, pad=7, labelsize=10)
    ax_right.plot(x, data[circle_column], linestyle="none", marker="o",
                  markersize=11, markerfacecolor="none",
                  markeredgecolor="black", markeredgewidth=1.6)
```

Each panel gets its own right-hand scale from 0 to 100 (see [A right-hand
scale](../techniques.qmd#sec-right-scale)).

The circles are drawn with `plot`, but with `linestyle="none"`, so only the
markers show. `markerfacecolor="none"` leaves them hollow.

### The legend

```python
legend_handles = [
    Line2D([], [], linestyle="none", marker="s", markersize=8,
           markerfacecolor="none", markeredgecolor="black"),
    Line2D([], [], linestyle="none", marker="o", markersize=8,
           markerfacecolor="none", markeredgecolor="black"),
]
axes[1].legend(legend_handles, ["Percent of GDP", "Percent of exports\n(right scale)"],
               loc="upper left", bbox_to_anchor=(0.0, 1.01), fontsize=9,
               handletextpad=0.3, labelspacing=0.4)
```

The bars have two colours (one per country), so a coloured box in the legend
would be misleading. As in the published chart, the legend uses black
outlines: an open square (`marker="s"`) for the bars and an open circle for
the circles. It is placed only in the right-hand panel (`axes[1]`). See
[Legends](../techniques.qmd#sec-legends).

## The complete script

The full `python/fig-1-3-1.py`, as it runs:

```` {.python filename="python/fig-1-3-1.py"}
"""Figure 1.3.1: Exports of Goods (two panels)."""
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D
from matplotlib.ticker import MultipleLocator

from chart_style import add_right_axis, new_chart, read_chart_data, save_chart

STEM = "fig-1-3-1"

bar_colours = {"Mexico": "#08649B", "Canada": "#CB6418"}

# Each panel: (data sheet, panel title, bar column, circle column).
panels = [
    ("datal", "Canada and Mexico Exports\nto the United States",
     "(% GDP)", "(% goods exports)"),
    ("datar", "United States Exports to\nCanada and Mexico",
     "Percent of GDP", "Percent of exports (right scale)"),
]

fig, axes = new_chart(
    title="Exports of Goods",
    subtitle=None,
    caption="Sources: Haver Analytics; national authorities; and IMF staff calculations.",
    title_size=14,
    caption_size=9.5,
    left=0.35,
    right=0.35,
    top_gap=0.55,
    bottom_gap=0.45,
    ncols=2,
    wspace=0.75,
)

for ax, (sheet, panel_title, bar_column, circle_column) in zip(axes, panels):
    data = read_chart_data(STEM, sheet)
    x = range(len(data))

    # Bars: percent of GDP, on the left scale.
    ax.bar(x, data[bar_column], width=0.56,
           color=[bar_colours[c] for c in data["category"]])
    ax.set_xticks(x, data["category"])
    ax.set_xlim(-0.78, len(data) - 0.22)
    ax.set_ylim(0, 40)
    ax.yaxis.set_major_locator(MultipleLocator(10))
    ax.tick_params(axis="x", length=0, pad=7, labelsize=10)
    ax.tick_params(axis="y", direction="in", length=2.3, pad=7, labelsize=10)
    ax.set_title(panel_title, loc="left", color="#7F7F7F", fontweight="bold",
                 fontsize=11.5, linespacing=0.95, pad=14)

    # Circles: percent of exports, on the right scale.
    ax_right = add_right_axis(ax, (0, 100), 25)
    ax_right.tick_params(axis="y", direction="in", length=2.3, pad=7, labelsize=10)
    ax_right.plot(x, data[circle_column], linestyle="none", marker="o",
                  markersize=11, markerfacecolor="none",
                  markeredgecolor="black", markeredgewidth=1.6)

# Legend, in the right-hand panel.
legend_handles = [
    Line2D([], [], linestyle="none", marker="s", markersize=8,
           markerfacecolor="none", markeredgecolor="black"),
    Line2D([], [], linestyle="none", marker="o", markersize=8,
           markerfacecolor="none", markeredgecolor="black"),
]
axes[1].legend(legend_handles, ["Percent of GDP", "Percent of exports\n(right scale)"],
               loc="upper left", bbox_to_anchor=(0.0, 1.01), fontsize=9,
               handletextpad=0.3, labelspacing=0.4)

save_chart(fig, STEM)
````
